items.d: A fortune coin used as an amulet by most bounty hunters. When these coins appear, it means their luck has run out.
items.u: Can be exchanged for all kinds of supplies.

items.d: Good job. Keep it up and get stronger. As long as you don't give up, your efforts will pay off in the end.
items.u: Experience gained from battle. It shows how far you've come.

items.d: Haste makes waste. For Rhodes Island, every operation has the potential for a loss of life. Therefore, it is wise to drill before actual combat, long before we run into an enemy ambush.
items.u: A plan used for tactical drills. Use it on the operation interface to simulate a battle so you can make plans accordingly.

items.d: 'What is it that distinguishes us from this land? Our breath, or feeling? Or life and death?'
items.u: The mental capacity to remain self aware, draw up plans, and execute them.

items.d: The elimination of chaos does not necessarily ensure the establishment of order. 'Natural disasters turn into man-made disasters,' but the Contingency Contract system at least provides you with a solution.
items.u: A symbol of cooperation. Can be used to unlock additional content in Contingency Contract.

items.d:
An auxiliary function of Rhodes Island's intelligence processing system. After extracting effective intelligence from a mass of information, the system is able to recreate images of past events. Information extracted through crystallization is typically of greater importance.
Its synthesis into optical disc form is simply for easier understanding by the layperson.
items.u: A topological model of aggregated information. Can be used to rebuild past events.

items.d: Credit holds communities together and stands as a symbol of social stability. Sometimes it's even more valuable than money, so do please cherish it.
items.u: A token of friendship. Can be used to exchange items from the Store.
items.o: Friend Support, Support Units, Dormitory Ambience, Clue Exchange

items.d:
Snack bags usually are not a very effective way to preserve the integrity of their contents, so it's hard to find one with a complete cookie inside.
Though a bit fragmented, the overall appearance is cute enough, and the flavor is still uncompromised.
items.u: Sold exclusively at Peterheim Middle School and all the rage among students, can be exchanged for various supplies.

items.d: Vouchers with no worth anywhere outside of Caladon. These roughly printed vouchers prop up the lives of everyone in the Infected community.
items.u: Vouchers for material supplies issued by Caladon City to its Infected workers. Can purchase a multitude of goods at thrift shops that the government will not provide.

items.d: The original owners of these antique coin have long departed from this remote land. However, the descendants of these decorated nobles still demanded Wolumonde's respect, and thus they passed into law the ability to circulate these coins for the purpose of satisfying their vanity.
items.u: An antique currency that is still in circulation in Wolumonde; Can be used to exchange for rewards at the August Fair.

items.u: An antique currency that is still in circulation in Wolumonde; Can be used to exchange for rewards at the August Fair.

items.d: Grip this document within your hands as if the distinctive laws of Leithanien never wavered. But, this illusion has long been shattered by the tragedy unfolding before your eyes in Wolumonde - delve deep into the mines, woods, and unclaimed vales, and bring justice to the perpetrators.
items.u: A warrant issued by Wolumonde's Gendarmerie, authorizing entry into occupied zones to hunt down ruffians who fled amidst the chaos.

items.d: With this library card, you can read any story that piques your interest. No matter what events may ensue, the time that you spend will all be recorded.
items.u: A library card independently issued by the private library. Can be used to read any material, however no items may be removed from the premises.

items.d: Originally seen only in Zumama's tribe, these eventually scattered throughout various places in the rainforests and wilds. Each one seems imaginative to the point of defying the laws of physics, but falls short of the industrial standards of any country.
items.u: Widely-used mechanical parts in Zumama's tribe, can be exchanged for various supplies.

items.d: Allows you to blur the boundary between fact and fiction, seeing things that you could not see before. Of course, this is the culprit behind your adventures.
items.u: These psychadelic-looking mushrooms exuding brilliant colors can enhance the performance of the Limbic System.

items.d: Ceobe's favorite food. She is willing to part with anything in exchange for these.
items.u: A traditional Minosian food made from starch and fructose. Used to obtain rewards from the Honey Biscuit Castle.

items.d: The fast rusting remains of war ambitions, Knightclub knockouts, or perhaps damaged weapon parts. Poses a risk of Originium infection if not handled properly. For some strange reason, occasionally found in common working-class households.
items.u: A type of worn-out mechanical part commonly found around Dzwonek, recyclable at city supermarkets across Kazimierz.

items.d: Every medal represents Ch'en's swift mid-investigation resolution of incidents unrelated to her assignment from Ms. Candela. During the time she was retained in Dossoles, the city's crime rate reached a record low. As a warning for the local police department, these Ch'en medals have been displayed in the middle of the head office, where you can't miss them.
items.u: Medals specially ordered by Ms. Candela to be cast to commend Ch'en's actions. Accumulate certain amounts and the Dossoles Police Station will issue rewards.

items.d: Mama John's of Columbia has been offering industrial assembly-line products for all trades, all walks and all rhythms of life in a capacity Bolívar's native industry can't compare to, to the extent that all these vouchers, originally simply issued to promote sales, have become more and more truly valuable. At times, they even serve as the currency for dealings between local small-time gangs.
items.u: Vouchers redeemable at all Mama John's in Dossoles.

items.u: Vouchers redeemable at all Mama John's in Dossoles.

items.d: At the time, Hoshiguma and Swire weren't aware of how they'd handily sorted out Ch'en's objective. The only reason they never ran into her was because Swire immediately dragged Hoshiguma off to go shopping.
items.u: A commemoration of Ch'en's special investigation in Dossoles.

items.d: That day, that moment Ch'en and Lin Yühsia came out of the A.H.C. Bar, the gunpowder tension between them had everyone following the championship excited beyond belief.
items.u: A commemoration of Ch'en's special investigation in Dossoles.

items.d: In Swire's belief, she needs a partner just as Hoshiguma is to Ch'en, and simultaneously, she believes Lin Yühsia could become that partner. She's made no small effort to see that happen, and ultimately, you can tell how it turned out just by the look on their faces.
items.u: A commemoration of Ch'en's special investigation in Dossoles.

items.d: Though when she set off to return to Rhodes Island, Ch'en didn't fully understand the city of Dossoles, neither does she believe there'll come a day she truly does. That said, she'll always remember this place.
items.u: A commemoration of Ch'en's special investigation in Dossoles.

items.d: A once treasured clock, now reduced to nothing more than a broken dial with some small value only to collectors. You find things like this in abandoned houses. A clock silently keeping the time can be priceless, or worthless. The hour hand on the dial is stuck in place, vainly trying to turn.
items.u: An old, broken piece of a clock that can be exchanged for supplies at the weekend yard sale. Someone will want it.

items.d: A couple blond Fortes are selling gold pieces of paper at three times the stated price. This voucher can be used to buy aid packages for competition knights in the arena, or as a bankroll to bet on, but be prepared to pay more than the number printed on it. A piece of paper, a huge sum, a knight's life of honor and shame.
items.u: A new securitized holding launched by the Mieszko Group that allows you to buy souvenirs at a Kazimierz duty free shop.
items.o: Event Stage drop, Event mission reward

items.d:
This weekend, the L.G.D. is joining hands with our local stray animal shelters to hold an adoption drive. We hope all our friends in the city able to adopt will jump at the opportunity to give these homeless little ones a chance at a brand new life.
Of course, those who aren't in a position to adopt can still contribute by offering cans of pet food, not to mention the splendid gifts awaiting anyone who donates.
items.u: A tin of pet food common to the Lungmen market, cheap and delicious. Just give the ring pull a flick, and you'll have your little dear bounding over to you.

items.d: Within this building of money and power, the tired form of your face serves absolutely no use, vocalizations and brain-thoughts all the more insignificant. In here, only status matters.
items.u: An ID card granting free access in the General Chamber of Commerce, signaling greater privileges to be open to Rhodes Island.
items.o: Acquiring certain prestige in the event

items.d: The file manager in the darkness has another duty: to cleverly let 'secrets' be found by those in the know. The Adeptus Sprawiedliwi have never given up their control of Kazimierz—whether good or ill.
items.u: A key that can open the underground gate of the Wall of Champions exhibit hall, unlocking some additional information.
items.o: Acquiring certain prestige in the event

items.d: The people use these shining fluorescent lamps to subdue nightfall, such is the light of Kazimierz. In civilized lands, traveling bards sing of gold, wandering knights forced to battle sword with glass. Indifferent are the silent waves; on this small, final vessel, she dredged up glory.
items.u: A scale miniature of the Land of the Knights, often elaborately laid out in the decorative cases of parlors.
items.o: Event Stage drop, Event mission reward

items.u: A scale miniature of the Land of the Knights, often elaborately laid out in the decorative cases of parlors.

items.d: A wellbeing charm hand-carved by the Moushan villagers to pray for blessings. Take it to Yishan Temple, have the censer acolyte bestow it a stroke of cinnabar, and it may put you all the more at ease.
items.u: A plaque carved of crude peachwood. When a year's harvest is good, some are willing to exchange their foodstuffs with the elderly, whose consummate craft produces these charms, by which auspiciousness is sought.

items.d: Kjeragandr's will dwells within. Kjerag's people pray to these, to be blessed and for good health.
items.u: A sacred stone blessed by a member of the Vine-Bead Court. Collect a certain amount to exchange with the people for goods.

items.d: You can make them during factory work hours, but it's no easy thing to sneak them off. They work as weapons as well as currency, and act as one measure of status in the prison.
items.u: A currency universally recognized amongst the prisoners. Can be used through secret channels to obtain what you want.
items.o: Event Stage drop, Event mission reward

items.d: Landscape postcards independently published by the people all over, known for their distinct and bold framing, all using photos chosen from personal submissions, with some small fame among a subset of collectors. Different stories take root in different lands, and the scenery is always there to tell without a word.
items.u: Postcards printed with unique landscapes from every part, allowing a taste of all their sceneries without having to set foot outside. Can be used to exchange for goods with the staff of branch offices everywhere.

items.evName: The Black Forest Wills A Dream
items.d: So that others may more easily find supplies hidden in the forest, the hunters have made simple waymarkers. Be sure to restock some too after you avail of them, for the trees know all.
items.u: A crude carving left behind by the hunters. Wooden figures with indistinct features reach forth an arm, pointing to caves stockpiled with food, remedies, and tools.

items.d: Diligent workers step hurriedly, easy-to-carry jarred tea there in times of need. The tea is chosen with care, pure in color and scent, flavor sweet and light and long-lasting, aftertaste melodious. Numerous brands exist, standing their own ground in drinks sections of supermarkets in every region of Yan, save for Zhe'ergen Signature, which no one pays any mind.
items.u: A specialty jarred beverage common in Shangshu. They say it always sells out at inns and teahouses.
items.o: Event Stage drop, Event mission reward

items.d: On its front, 'starshrouded snow' is engraved in characters from ancient times. Just the talent to create these inksticks can be called rare. Dusk very rarely uses normal inksticks. If she's out of options, employing one to depict one and retrieving one fresh isn't impossible either.
items.u: Dusk's handmade inkstick. Nobody knows how they're made. Perhaps you can make use of them to ask her about a few things.
items.o: Event Stage drop, Event mission reward

items.d: Bottletree sap naturally fermented in the abdomens of tree-hanging Originium slugs, celebrated by man and adored by sandbeasts. Still, how the beasts get the sap when they can't climb trees is one of Rim Billiton's great mysteries. Are there feral barreners helping them? Can't be...
items.u: Extremely spicy and fantastically invigorating, with a deep velvet flavor fresh bottletree sap can't hope to match. And the upside of not chronically ruining your body like hard liquor would. Give it to wild sandbeasts, and you might end up trading for their stashed curios.

items.d: The collectability of a bullet depends on its caliber size. As to why an empty shell can be traded for goods in a dessert shop—You must understand that, as the most popular destination among locals, Lateranian Desserts has always been more than just a dessert shop.
items.u: A collectible somewhat popular among Laterans. Collect enough to exchange with the dessert shop owner for goods.
items.o: Event Stage drop, Event mission reward

items.d: The certificate bears the signature of the administrator, an anti-counterfeiting watermark, and a detailed record of the supplies needed by the operators and for what reasons they are needed. After these three items have been verified, the responsible personnel will collect the voucher attached to the certificate and distribute the supplies to the field operator.
items.u: Rationing certificates issued by Rhodes Island to field operators, including vouchers. Can be used to exchange for supplies in Rhodes Island's landship, regional branches, and various safehouses.
items.o: Event Stage drop, Event mission reward

items.d: A large piece of slag that was ejected from the Soul Furnace for unknown reasons, which shattered into pieces when bombarded by the airship. It contains trace amounts of Originium and Oriron, but extraction is extremely difficult.
items.u: Fireworks pieces that fell from the sky. The custodian of a certain furnace node is looking for it, but what you get in return for it seems to differ from person to person.

items.d: The Iberians of times past guided their course by compass, the needle bearing the weight of their wild ambitions and golden dreams. Naught but ravings nowadays; the needle is broken, the brass is tarnished, and none know the dreadnought's end, bar the silent sea.
items.u: All attempts to tread unto the sea have been vain and futile. Where the compass points is certain to be anguished, turbid, and sunken.

items.d: Mineral, flora, fauna, cities; vestiges of life, and even symbols of civilization. In the meanders of this time overflowing with Originium, countless things fade from Terra's boundless history of organic evolution. Disasters unfold unabatingly, and even the grandest cities all disappear in the end. But there will always be people to record it all. She will come in her slow walk with time.
items.u: Specimen sketches scattered all over the ground in a great gale. If you help tidy them up, you can earn some supplies.
items.o: Event Stage drop, Event mission reward

items.d: A shattered yet still brilliant crystal shaped like a petal, often seen among death-blackened scorched earth. They are ripples left behind by traveling Canoes, engraved with the final memories and emotions of those who passed away.
items.u: A crystal of blood left behind in the battlefield ruins. It is said that if you place it in a deserted nook where roses bloom, when the twin moons are at their brightest, the fortunate will find some unexpected presents waiting for them come daybreak.

items.d: The notes scribbled on the staff are jumbled and disorderly. Only the composer himself can, at a glance, make out the soul hidden therein.
items.u: Musicians often misplace their drafts during outbursts of emotion. If you straighten it out and return it to its owner, perhaps you will receive a new piece in return.
items.o: Event Stage drop, Event mission reward

items.d: A small object on the cusp of becoming a geist, taking advantage of humanity's inattention to trundle about. Pranks on the street corner, odd sounds from the depths of stoves... A strange air permeates the town.
items.u: If you bring lost geists that have not yet transformed to Mr. Pu's place, he will give you a few interesting trinkets in return as thanks. You notice the things he previously collected all have their own names.

items.d: Very sensitive to neural activity, and can replace some of the functions of traditional Arts Units. In the Rhine Lab Defense Section's laboratory supplies management handbook, this test reagent's hazard and confidentiality levels are both listed at maximum.
items.u: The latest innovation of Rhine Lab's Energy Section. Collect enough and exchange with the Laboratory Recycling Depot for goods.
items.o: Event Stage drop, Event mission reward

items.d: The cards might be small, but get enough of them and you can trade them in for big prizes!
items.u: A reward for first clearing stages which can be used to buy prizes at the Exchange Counter; subsequent reclears will not reward more.

items.d: Medals prepared by Rhodes Island's workshop for operators participating in Stronghold Protocol. Magnetic. Apparently, if you gather enough of them, you can make a fortress out of chess pieces.
items.u: Can be exchanged for all sorts of supplies in Stronghold Protocol.
items.o: Event Stage drop, Event mission reward

items.d: Right and wrong are far from crucial in a simulation. They are only a form of support. They help you make the correct choices when the battle is real.
items.u: Experience gained from finished trials. Upgrades trial levels.
items.o: Event Stage drop, Event mission reward

items.d: An encrypted data block. Always remember, the conversion of information often entails unavoidable wear. Make good use of your information storage devices, but do not depend on them.
items.u: Used to perform Data Iteration on Limiter Units.

items.d: An ordinary floor sign. After being used to denote acceleration points in stool racing competitions, operators interested in these competitions have become rather fond of it, eventually turning it into a collectible.
items.u: Can be exchanged at Breakthrough Milestones for rewards.

items.d: Rhodes Island issues special reward points as an incentive to field operators dispatched to the base building operation in Szubat-Arsalan. These points can be used to redeem important supplies.
items.u: Can be exchanged for the corresponding event stage reward.
items.o: Limited-time Event Missions, Daily Event Missions

items.evName: Grani and the Knights' Treasure - Rerun
items.d: A fortune coin used as an amulet by most bounty hunters. When these coins appear, it means their luck has run out.
items.u: Can be exchanged for all kinds of supplies.

items.d: Apparently, using it can send a fullscreen fireworks effect along with a message to the entire Duel Channel. But what the richie-riches who break the TOS to spam them in public chat all day might not know is that they can be blocked with a click of a button on the website.
items.u: One of the more expensive Duel Channel gifts, and can be exchanged on the website for material rewards, with free shipping and home delivery.

items.d: Points gained for taking down OpFor troops, awarded to competitors in the form of medals. Owing to it being forged by Minos smiths, in each medal's engraving is the proverb 'all heroes arise from normal people.'
items.u: A small medal made from metal. Gain certain amounts and receive corresponding competition rewards.
items.o: Event Stage drop, Event mission reward

items.d: A flickering, glinting fragment. A light so that you no longer fear the dark as you walk dauntlessly on through the thorns.
items.u: Can be exchanged for Milestone Rewards.
items.o: From event-exclusive drops and event missions

items.d: WARNING: For best results, administer via peripheral IV. In case of first-aid, can attempt via CVC. If shock ensues after first dose, second IV may be administered within 5-7 minutes (repeat dose). EACH DOSE COULD BE THE KEY TO SAVING A LIFE IN THE FIELD. MAKE GOOD USE OF THEM.
items.u: A new formulation from Rhodes Island's Medical R&D, capable of temporarily suppressing the exacerbation of Oripathy in Catastrophe- or battlefield-level Originium zones. THIS DRUG PLACES IMMENSE STRAIN ON THE BODY. USE WITH CAUTION.

items.d: A certificate of participation in Rhodes Island's Icebreaker Games. 'Leave your sweat in the stadium. Come home with camaraderie.'
items.u: As you collect Participation Certificates, so does Hype. Reach certain Hype levels to receive rewards.

items.evName: Reclamation Algorithm - Fire Within the Sand
items.d: Life prospers, age passes down to age, and this is their proof.
items.u: Can be exchanged at milestones for rewards.

items.d: The Icebreaker Games have the spotlight today thanks to your wholehearted support.
items.u: Can be exchanged for the corresponding event stage reward.

items.u: Can be used to promote Operators in Rebuilding Mandate.

items.d: The most important things in the Frontier Outposts are courage, perseverance, and humility. Live, learn, produce.
items.u: Can be used to increase Operator training level in Rebuilding Mandate.

items.d: Building and producing is no less a chore than fighting and killing. Remain vigilant and work together.

items.d:
Virtual marker with Closure's crypto-signature. The quantity deployed is carefully calculated, ensuring that aid provided by Rhodes Island HQ is utilized efficiently.
'More interesting than a plain paper production plan, don't you think?'
items.u: Can be used to apply Construction Strategies in Rebuilding Mandate.

items.d:
Rhodes Island was not built in a day, but we build it up day by day.
'For Rhodes Island.'
items.u: Credits derived from total resources, which can be used to obtain rewards from Closure.

items.d: The big prizes demand far too many corks in exchange. The vast majority will trade in for a few mismatched tasting wineglasses at best. It is a blatantly Kazimierzian marketing ploy, but that has not deterred Golden Prairie from relying on it to open up the Nuova Volsiniese market.
items.u: The cork stoppers Golden Prairie uses for red wine intended for the Nuova Volsiniese market, with a special seal stuck on top. Collect enough and exchange them at the Red Wine Championship Commission reception counter for prizes (such as tickets to watch the championship).

items.d: The pages retain handwriting of all shapes and sizes, the amount even serving to tell you how often the magazine's changed hands. Most of it is meaningless scrawls, but flashes of wisdom are scattered throughout.
items.u: Photocopies of a gaudy magazine, the contents preposterous, yet well-loved by Durin far and wide. Can be used at the Leaping Gloompincer Market to trade with the Durin for supplies.
items.o: Event Stage drop, Event mission reward

items.u: Pages filled with Taran folksongs and legends, copied down as heard. Collect enough, and you'll be able to trade them with the River Valley Caravan for goods.

items.d: A Yumen specialty product, high-purity spirit. Beloved by all drinkers, brewed by all brewers. A brew mixed of sandstorms on the border, and sun beating down in the sky and wind on the poplars, one gulp is a throat of blades and a drink of fire, and even the chilliest nights need no longer be feared.
items.u: Take a jar of freshly brewed spirit, and trade it with the old smith for a newly-edged sword of fine craft. 'Blood for water, wine for a blade. A close friend crossed by, grace and vengeance all too willing.'

items.u: A common low-grade material usable in Alchemy.
items.o: Event Stage drop, Event mission reward

items.d: The hard outer shell of an Originium Slug covered in tiny clusters of Originium. Tastes slightly bitter when licked. Even though there are many types of Originium Slugs out there, the quality of the materials they yield doesn't vary much at all.
items.u: A regular material usable in Alchemy, obtainable by putting in just a little bit of work.
items.o: Event Stage drop, Event mission reward

items.d: The sharp fangs of an Oxmane, so sharp that they can tear apart flesh with ease. They serve as an excellent Alchemy material. As a reminder, they must not be used in place of dentures.
items.u: A fine material usable in Alchemy, obtainable by putting in a fair amount of work.
items.o: Event Stage drop, Event mission reward

items.d: The thick hide of Direswines, elastic and able to withstand great impact force. To obtain this material, one must first go through very intense battles. It takes lots of effort to get a taste of Direswine rind jelly.
items.u: A rare, high-grade material usable in Alchemy.
items.o: Event Stage drop, Event mission reward

items.d: A kind of crystal as clear as tears. Supposedly, they formed in the carcasses of a now extinct creature. When observed closely under light, you can even see the stars flow and circulate.
items.u: An extremely rare, top-of-the-line material usable in Alchemy.
items.o: Event Stage drop, Event mission reward

items.d: A rare gem that occasionally grows in the wyvern's body. Hunters who are lucky enough to get their hands on them often find themselves hesitant when processing them.
items.u: A material obtainable from battling a Rathalos. Perfect as melding material.
items.o: Event Stage drop, Event mission reward

items.d: Aside from the data hidden by Nasti all over the lands, new data are continually produced with the federal government's support. Columbia is gradually realizing the value of Kristen's research.
items.u: A chip containing flight data recorded at various altitudes and environments. Collect a certain amount to exchange with the Special Case Contact C.U.D.O.D. for goods.
items.o: Event Stage drop, Event mission reward

items.u: Statues of saints bearing guns were once ornamental mainstays all over the monastery, but most are now nowhere to be seen. The monastery's devout followers are willing to barter what supplies they have in exchange for these fragments.

items.d: Plastics, paper, wood... even scrapped Originium circuitry. Their only commonality is that they all burn when thrown in the power plant, and provide the plate with just that much more heat.
items.u: Combustibles salvaged from Davistown and its environs. Practically worthless for heat, and produces way too much smoke, but fuel is fuel and there's an old worker by the energy tower who'll trade goods from the mine for it.

items.d: An ordinary floor sign. After being used to denote acceleration points in stool racing competitions, operators interested in these competitions have become rather fond of it, eventually turning it into a collectible.
items.u: Can be exchanged at Breakthrough Milestones for rewards.

items.d: Apparently, using it can send a fullscreen fireworks effect along with a message to the entire Duel Channel. But what the richie-riches who break the TOS to spam them in public chat all day might not know is that they can be blocked with a click of a button on the website.
items.u: One of the more expensive Duel Channel gifts, and can be exchanged on the website for material rewards, with free shipping and home delivery.

items.d: To help calm the children anxious about leaving the landship, Raidian made these pin badges with paging and messaging functionalities, encouraging them to keep on smiling and stay in contact. After hearing about them, many operators asked her for some, recording words of encouragement on them before hiding them all over prior to the evacuation.
items.u: Communicators made by Raidian in the shape of pin badges. Retrieving them can help reduce interference on the comms network, and they can be traded at Closure's for all sorts of supplies.

items.d: A certificate of participation in Rhodes Island's Icebreaker Games. 'Leave your sweat in the stadium. Come home with camaraderie.'
items.u: As you collect Participation Certificates, so does Hype. Reach certain Hype levels to receive rewards.

items.d: As you collect Mementos, so does Hype. Reach certain Hype levels to receive rewards.

NOTE: Pray faithfully to the newly erected Kjeragandr statue, and your odds of drawing the secret one go up!
items.u: Burdenbeast Blind Boxes—such a smash hit, Onboard Services ran out of stock for a time. That means this batch couldn't have come sooner, and the train attendants will be delighted to trade other goods for it.

items.u: An agricultural drone developed by the Tianshi Bureaus, which people occasionally leave lying in the fields after they malfunction. If you pick any up, you can exchange them for goods at Shennong Market.

items.o: Event Stage drop, Event mission reward

items.d: Crude sugar cubes of mechanized make, a Babel wartime supply ration. Provides soldiers with ample energy and a hint of sweetness.
items.u: A 'hard currency' aboard Babel. Save up enough to spare, and the nice Vampire lady down by the Engineering Team will trade for some scarcities you'll appreciate.

items.u: Fine grains of gems that glitter like stars in the sky, older than the City of Radiance, and brighter than its hidden treasures.

items.d:
An emblem personally gifted by the Madam Speaker for outstanding behavior during battle or reconstruction. Anyone can use them as valuable tokens of opposition during the notice periods of the proposals deciding Londinium's future.
Note that Parliament strictly forbids the trading of this honor!
items.u: Every respectable citizen has the right to oppose Parliament's public proposals, and these emblems are Parliament's acknowledgment of said right. But rumor has it that some civil servants at the Office of Proposed Resolutions will secretly trade goods for this valuable right?

items.u: Reward obtained by completing Pinch-Out Experimental Operation. Can be exchanged for supplies.

items.u: Invitations handed out by an anonymous figure at Carnevale. You can exchange them for generous gifts at any Fiera delle Meraviglie Notturne. Relax, once people see the invitation, you will receive a warm welcome.

items.u: Both the daily drink of the pirates of the Salt Flat, and a currency they accept. So long as the fleet lacks priceless treasures such as rum, it will never be replaced.

items.d: The sound of hitting flint fades into the vast snow. The darkness is boundless, with only a tiny speck of flame to illuminate it, quietly flickering and melting the ice and snow, and waiting for the sun to rise again.
items.u: An indispensable tool in the wilderness of Ursus, lighting the flame that drives back the cold and darkness. Fire is banned in the mines, but that has not stopped the miners from sharing flints.

items.evName: Such is the Joy of Our Reunion
items.d: Fragrant meals fear not alleys deep. While invisible to the eye on most days, there is a faint aroma lining the streets, at least until it hits you face-first in front of the restaurant it leads to. You need only follow the scent of food to paint a grand picture of Baizao's streets.
items.u: Don't be stingy when it comes to complimenting how the food smells at Savors at Yu's. Once the Young Chef's ears go red from praise, he'll discreetly add a few extra bits of meat to your plate.

items.u: A damaged Originium lamp found in the Dark Woods. Once Na Saoirsí's supply issues were resolved, the citizens spontaneously decided to organize, taking out the only supplies they had on hand to recover these relics of the war.

items.d: 'WARNING! Please refrain from undue perception of/empathy with simulation products, or subsequent generation of false data may lead to irreversible mental damage.'
items.u: Stores operation data from the Formulative Battlerealm. Accumulate to advance Cogitative Diving Evaluation progress.

items.d: A pacifier soaked in saliva, with a miniature halo atop it. The child who threw it away is now wailing incessantly. Guide the way for the lost pacifier, and it will return to the child's side.
items.u: The enlightenment of the Shrine of Nurtury has spread like wildfire, and both the living and the unliving have sprouted halos. The first pacifiers to receive them wandered off through the Shrine in their confusion, leaving countless babes to suffer restless nights. If you are able to return them to their posts, the beleaguered nurturers will be happy to give gifts as thanks.
items.o: Event Stage drop, Event mission reward

items.d: What is it, really? A ghost? A prop? A hallucination? Somebody's Friedkin pet? Nobody knows. Miss.Christine simply waves her twin tails as she languidly basks in the sunlight.
items.u: Despite the hellish workload and a high-pressure film set, the mysterious black shadow never fails to show up every now and again, to the point that the overwhelmed crew have started to wildly speculate who is behind it. If you can trace the whereabouts of the 'Phantom of the Studio', they will be very grateful.
items.o: Event Stage drop, Event mission reward

items.d: Fragmentary words from the streets. They may seem useless, but they hide threads leading to all sorts of secrets. To those who know how to make use of them, even the smallest whisper of gossip can be a stepping stone to business.
items.u: Used at the Soudanshitsu to start business for the day. The juicy stories you hear every day all start with a chat, after all.

items.d: A lottery ticket, the prize being admission to a certain performer's 'graduation' farewell concert. While the event was officially canceled, it is still in private circulation among fans, a memento of a turning point in her career.
items.u: A ticket distributed by a talent agency, which can be exchanged for entry into a lottery. After a certain incident, they were the hottest item at the Vintage Bazaar for a while, and could be traded for nearly anything.
items.o: Event Stage drop, Event mission reward

items.d: No matter its beauty, a dream is but a dream, destined to fade from memory in time. It is hence that the masters of the Castle of Dreams have made a museum to hold onto these vanishing dreams, storing them in the manner of precious works of art. Each master has their own tastes, so take care not to offend with what you give them.
items.u: A piece of a dream-shaped puzzle, dazzling and beautiful. You found these strewn across the floor when you came to the Castle. Now, be patient, gather them together, and see the wondrous scenes you bring to life once more.

items.d: A survey instrument developed by Rhine Lab specifically for use in Kjerag to collect various data from the mysterious snowy realm, maintaining stable functionality even in low-temperature environments. 'Myths are merely unexplained realities, and science will one day snatch off their veils.'—Elena firmly believes in this.
items.u: Multi-functional survey equipment scattered throughout the snow from the avalanches. Please return it to the observation station when found, and the staff will express their gratitude with practical supplies.

items.d: It's just cheap sugar water based on Forte Energy Drinks' flavoring? Who cares! Nowadays, you only hear such boring truths from bitter and bankrupt companies that didn't think of bottling their beverages in rocket-shaped containers.
items.u: An innovative beverage inspired by high-altitude air-supply devices, now the lifeblood of Columbians. No one would refuse to fork over a high price to taste a new era beyond the Starpod.

items.d: Even though everyone has a terminal loaded with all kinds of apps these days, the Minoans still prefer to follow their ancient traditions.

items.d:
An auxiliary function of Rhodes Island's intelligence processing system. After extracting effective intelligence from a complex batch of information, the system was able to recreate images of past events with astonishing fidelity.
The information was packaged as videotapes to make it easier for ordinary people to understand.
items.u: A topological model of effective intelligence that can be used to reconstruct past events.

items.d: Once, they said it was the origin of suffering. Now, they say its disappearance was the beginning of tragedy.
items.u: A piece of deactivated Originium that no longer has any practical value, even if it is polished into the shape of an Originite Prime.

items.d: People speculate as to who its master was. It has been passed from one person to another, carrying more and more stories, the culmination of the miners' lives.
items.u: An abandoned mining lamp that still works, though the name tag has been torn off.

items.d: The nobles of Grypherburg see this symbol as a grave threat, but it was from their hubris that it came about in the first place.
items.u: The flag of Ursus with the mark of Reunion painted over it. Defacing the national flag is punishable by death according to the Flag Law of Ursus.

items.d: The corruption of the empire may not have begun with Grypherburg, but its decline surely started with a dud from Tulskaya.

items.d: Based on a massive volume of live combat records, PRTS can perfectly replicate your tactics to conduct Annihilation and Stationary Security Service missions by proxy, using actuarial data processing, logic training, and scenario simulation. You're spared even the need to pay it your full attention.

items.d: A new material still in the experimental stage. Not only can it output large amounts of energy, but it can also adapt to Originium Arts. This may indicate the future development of this optically protective material.
items.u: A product of cutting-edge research on luminescent materials. Can be used for high level upgrades.

items.d: A material that possesses a molecular recognitive capacity under specific high-temperature conditions. Can selectively adsorb Originium when used as a reagent, allowing for precise handling of Originium materials, lower Originium device energy consumption, and the opening of further new possibilities.
items.u: A product of modern technology that requires the ultimate in industrial craft. Used in advanced strengthening projects.

items.d: A crystallization of Terra's Originium technology. A symbol of Terra's industrial modernization. From Originium Casting units to intercity network servers, their making all starts with inventions like these.
items.u: An expensive Originium industry product. Can be used for major upgrades.

items.d: This material can deliver Originium Arts smoothly and its amazing hardness makes it impossible to penetrate. It will set a new standard for weapon materials.
items.u: An artificial metal that doesn't exist in nature. Can be used for high level upgrades.

items.d: A device that is sensitive to Originium within a certain range. It can significantly improve the sensitivity of nearby weapons and equipment to Originium, making them near vessels for Originium Arts.
items.u: The brainchild of modern science and industry. Can be used for high level upgrades.

items.d: A material commonly used as an isolation coating for delicate equipment. Its bonding effect is strong enough to interrupt the volatilization of Originium.
items.u: A complicated liquid industrial product. Can be used for high level upgrades.

items.d: An optical material that boasts both physical durability and astonishing Originium Arts resistance, currently used in studies regarding optical protection. Other uses are still being tested.
items.u: A specialized material that displays useful optical qualities and other physical traits. Can be used for high level upgrades.

items.d: A particle that can adsorb many different materials. At first, it was only used in cheap adsorbents, but has since become a cutting-edge material thanks to its strong universal coagulative properties.
items.u: A lab-made synthetic particle, boasting powerful adsorption properties. Can be used in a variety of strengthening projects.

items.d: An industrial product arrived at through the introduction of several excellent materials into the synthesis process, preserving luminous transmittance while vastly increasing strength and shock resistance. Prospects are high for its wide adoption in the field of defense.
items.u: A prefabricated industrial intermediate composed of multiple first-rate materials. Used in a variety of strengthening projects.

items.d: A novel transparent material born from the laboratory. Its high luminous transmittance and phenomenal durability in all aspects promise to make it an excellent substitute for many conventional materials.
items.u: A superlatively heat- and chemical-resistant industrial material. Used in a variety of strengthening projects.

items.d: A compound fiber board crafted through bespoke manufacturing. Exhibits outstanding functionality, both physically and chemically, coupled with a rarely-seen ease of processing. An irreplaceable part of many an industrial workflow.
items.u: A specialized fiber board, solidified in a mold. Used in a variety of strengthening projects.

items.d: A derived product in Originium engineering, widely used in industrial fields due to its exceptional functionality. In recent years, its unique appearance has also drawn keen interest from those working in design.
items.u: A specialized fiber bundle, possessing high tensile strength and elastic modulus. Used in a variety of strengthening projects.

items.d: A stable crystalline body, manufactured as a crystal blend within saturated solutions. Can provide materials with a diverse array of capabilities.
items.u: A compound crystal mass that has undergone high-tolerance refinement. Used in a variety of strengthening projects, and is a common material in synthetic items at factories.

items.d: The surface of this material has mutable characteristics, realizing results that were originally nearly impossible. CAUTION: industrial salt is not to be eaten under any circumstances.
items.u: A compound crystallization that has undergone low-tolerance refinement. Can be used in a variety of strengthening projects.

items.d: A biologically stable stock solution. Precautions should be taken to avoid cross-contamination during storage.
items.u: A stock solution prepared from a variety of active solvents. Can be used for high level upgrades.

items.d: Provides lubrication and heat resistance during the refining process, which can further increase the rate at which metal products meet final quality specifications.
items.u: An industrial agent necessary for metal processing. Can be used for a variety of upgrades.

items.d: A coating held together by high-molecule polymers. In addition to its baseline protective capabilities, it has also gained other special characteristics, of which heat resistance is but one of many.
items.u: A special coating made from a specific formulation process. Can be used for high level upgrades.

items.d: The product of a traditional solvent undergoing a modernization process, it demonstrates remarkably enhanced properties.
items.u: An active solvent with excellent physical characteristics, and good resistance to acids and bases. Can be used in a variety of upgrades.
